headline: Haiti Pressed, Scotland Punished
story: Haiti announced their tournament ambitions with a commanding display in Boston: 52% possession, 15 shots, sustained high pressing designed to suffocate Scotland's deep-sitting defense. But the match pivoted in the 28th minute, when Scotland broke through with a low-xG opportunity (0.14) that would prove decisive. Scotland offered little else—just nine shots and 1.1 high-press phases—and relied entirely on ruthlessness in transition to hold what they'd snatched.

The numbers revealed efficiency defeating dominance. Scotland's xG (0.91) exceeded Haiti's (0.7) on nine shots to Haiti's 15. In the decisive 28th minute, Scotland missed a big chance (0.58 xG) before converting a low-xG opportunity (0.14). Haiti's swift ball recovery (14.9 seconds to Scotland's 21.5) and 29 forced turnovers proved their press worked, yet they squandered crucial moments: a blocked chance (0.28 xG) in the 34th, and a saved chance (0.31 xG) in stoppage time. John McGinn (7.7) and Aaron Hickey (7.4) anchored Scotland's defense, while Hannes Delcroix (7.1) could not impose order on Haiti's attack.

keyMoment.text: Scotland's low-xG breakthrough settled a match where dominance met ruthlessness

home.verdict: Pressed high and controlled the match, but lacked precision in front of goal.
points: Only 2 of 15 shots on target—13% conversion rate cannot compete for three points
High press (4.7 phases) generated 29 forced turnovers; failed to convert chances
Swift ball recovery (14.9s) won the midfield battle but yielded no reward

away.verdict: Won with deep discipline and clinical ruthlessness against a superior opponent.
points: xG advantage (0.91 vs 0.7) on nine shots—efficiency over volume secured points
Minimal pressing (1.1 phases) absorbed Haiti's dominance and forced 35 turnovers
Survived a 0.58 xG miss at the 28th minute; clinical when the game opened

statLine: Haiti's 15 shots yielded just 2 on target and zero goals, while Scotland's nine shots and superior expected goals produced one clinical finish to decide a Group C contest between dominance and ruthlessness.
